findings.evidence: No off-device sink found for any of the three sources. ApplicationModule.kt:57: the 'StrictMode' match only registers StrictModeInitializer, whose body is behind if (false) (StrictModeInitializer.kt:13) and would only use penaltyLog. HistoricalProcessExitReasonsInitializer.kt:25-31: reads the last exit record through ActivityManager; the ANR trace is read and discarded (line 30, stackTrace?.length has no effect) and only reason and description go to logger.log (line 31). The logger is not a telemetry path: ApplicationModule.kt:48 provides LoggerImpl, and LoggerImpl.kt:14-23 keeps entries in an in-memory MutableSharedFlow (replay 100) and drops the params map. Its only production consumers of getLogFlow are DrawerFragment.kt:231 (on-screen log list), CameraFragment.kt:100-101 (Log.d to local logcat) and XoViewModel.kt:44-46 (on-screen UI state). No getLogsFlow consumer exists in production code. Build files (*.kts, *.toml, *.gradle) contain no Firebase, Crashlytics, AppMetrica, Sentry, Mixpanel, Amplitude, AppsFlyer, Bugsnag or Datadog dependency. Not inspected: the internals of androidx core-performance-play-services (libs.versions.toml:138), used by DevicePerformanceInitializer.kt:12-13; the app code only reads mediaPerformanceClass and passes it to the same local logger. Step 2 (disclosure search) skipped because is_transferred is false. Case 1.
findings.recommendation: No Data safety declaration is needed for performance diagnostics while the logger stays local, which matches the form's 'no data collected' answer. Any future crash or telemetry SDK, or a remote logger behind Logger, would require updating the form first. Optional hygiene: (1) SystemInfoInitializer.kt:14,20 puts ANDROID_ID into the log panel and, through CameraFragment.kt:101, into logcat; it stays on the device, but a persistent device identifier in logs would become a declarable identifier the moment logs are ever uploaded, so remove it. (2) Remove the dead code found here, per the project rule on unused code: the unused string at AD2AppInformation.kt:18, the if (false) block in StrictModeInitializer.kt:13 and the discarded trace read in HistoricalProcessExitReasonsInitializer.kt:29-30. findings.evidence: No user video leaves the device. RecorderCameraX.kt:72-83 records a 2-second clip to the app-private file filesDir/temp/CameraX-recording.mp4 (file.deleteOnExit() at line 75). The file is passed only through RecorderState.Completed (line 100) to Controller.startRecording (Controller.kt:92) and CameraViewModel.startRecording (CameraViewModel.kt:95-99), where it is stored in UI state as recordedFile. Its only reader in CameraFragment.kt:67-68 is commented out, so openVideo (line 72) is never called. VideoFragment.kt:34-39 uses android.widget.VideoView and MediaController to play a local Uri and has no network path. A search of feature/camera found no OkHttp, Retrofit, HttpURLConnection, URL(, multipart or upload usage. In addition, the camera module is not linked into the shipped app: app/build.gradle.kts lines 119-158 do not depend on projects.feature.camera, which is referenced only by feature/camera/demo and micro-benchmark. The AudioExoPlayer.kt match is a false positive for this data type: it plays audio only, from app-supplied response and item sound URLs (ResponsesFragment.kt:113, ItemInfoFragment.kt:79), not user videos.

findings.evidence: The app does not read or transmit the user's music files. AudioExoPlayer.kt:100-110 only plays a URI given to it, and its callers pass game audio: hero responses (ResponsesFragment.kt:113, item.audioUrl) and item sounds (ItemInfoFragment.kt:79). Network traffic here is an inbound download of public game audio, not an upload of user data. ResponseRingtoneSetter.kt:57-79 writes such a response into the shared MediaStore after a user action, and its query at lines 48-55 looks up only the app's own file by name in the AD2 folder. DownloadResponseManager.kt:109-136 getResponses is the only query that could list other audio on the device, but it is private, has no caller in that file, and its result is discarded. No READ_MEDIA_AUDIO or READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission appears in the module manifests. The other two matches are false positives: Motion.kt:90 'track' is trackPress, a touch gesture modifier, and VideoFragment.kt uses android.widget.MediaController for local video playback in a module not linked into the app.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for music. Remove the unused private getResponses and reSaveResponseIn methods from DownloadResponseManager.kt so that a future audit does not have to rule out the MediaStore audio query again.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): all three EMAILS evidence hits are false positives, the pattern 'imap' matched the word 'minimap' in hero icon asset paths.

findings.issue_summary: Data Safety Compliant (Local-Only): no user photo leaves the device. The parser hit is a developer tool that downloads game images, and the camera hits belong to a module the release app does not include and which has no network upload path.
findings.evidence: ImageUtils.kt:55 and :68 are an HTTP content-type default and an Accept header on a download of wiki/game images in the developer-only core/parser JVM tool: inbound game art, not a user's photos. FaceDetector.kt:7 (enum value CAMERA2) and CameraSettingsImpl.kt:17,19 (CameraSelector constants) are configuration with no image data. Forward trace of the camera path: StreamerCameraX.kt:85-90 turns frames into in-memory bitmaps and emits them on a local SharedFlow, Controller.kt:47-60 passes them to the on-device processor and into UI state, RecorderCameraX.kt writes a 2 second clip to context.filesDir/temp/CameraX-recording.mp4, and CameraFragment.kt:181-189 (class CameraX) writes a captured bitmap to local MediaStore. A search of feature/camera for OkHttp, Retrofit, HttpURLConnection, Ktor, sockets, upload, multipart, ACTION_SEND and Firebase Storage returned nothing. Its only network use visible in code is ONNXModelHub in ProcessorKotlinDL.kt:16-17, which loads a face-detection model (inbound) and sends no frames. Separately, app/build.gradle.kts declares no feature.camera dependency and app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml has no CAMERA entry; across all build files the only consumer outside feature/camera is micro-benchmark, as androidTestImplementation. So the CAMERA permission in manifest_details.json comes from feature/camera/ui/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml, aggregated across modules, and should not be in the release merged manifest. The app logger has no remote sink visible here (AppMetrica was removed in commit c05f7fe9d) and the camera feature logs no image data. ImagesCompressor.kt reads a content Uri but has no callers in app, feature or core, and writes only to app-specific external files.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for PHOTOS. Two optional checks: (1) this conclusion rests on the Gradle dependency graph, not on a built artifact, so confirm that android.permission.CAMERA is absent from the merged manifest of the release AAB before upload. (2) Under the project rule that unused code is deleted, remove ImagesCompressor.kt, which has no callers and would write user images to external files if it were ever wired in. If the camera module is added to the app later, re-audit it: CameraPermission.kt requests CAMERA and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, the face processing would need review under the Data Safety and sensitive-data rules, and the runtime model download would become a shipped network call.

findings.evidence: False positive for this data type. DrawerFragment.kt:181 calls packageManager.getPackageInfo(requireContext().packageName, 0).versionName, which reads only the app's own version and passes it to the DrawerMenu composable as the label "v$version" (line 188). It does not enumerate installed apps: no getInstalledPackages/getInstalledApplications at this site, and no QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES permission or <queries> element in any app manifest (the only <queries> is in macro-benchmark). findings.evidence: The permission is requested but no location is ever read. GamesFragment.kt:50 selects NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES on Android 13+ and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION only below it, because the platform requires that permission for Wi-Fi Direct peer discovery; the code comment on line 49 says so. The grant result goes only to viewModel.onWifiDirectPermission(granted) (lines 51, 65), a boolean forwarded to party.onWifiDirectPermission (GamesViewModel.kt:118). A search of main sources for LocationManager, FusedLocation, getLastKnownLocation, requestLocationUpdates and android.location returned no matches, and WifiDirectImpl.kt has no location access, so no coordinates exist to be sent. AppPermission.kt:11 belongs to the standalone demo app in feature/games/xo/demo, which app/build.gradle.kts does not depend on, so it does not ship in the release. It only checks and requests the permissions, then calls onPermissionGranted().
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for Precise location. Add android:maxSdkVersion="32" to ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION in feature/games/xo/domain/impl/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml (lines 11-16): the code requests location only below Android 13, and NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES already has neverForLocation. This keeps the location permission off newer devices and shrinks the permission surface. The request also fires in GamesFragment.onViewCreated (line 67) as soon as the screen opens, so consider explaining the Wi-Fi Direct reason first on Android 12 and lower, where users see a location prompt.

findings.evidence: These click handlers are navigation, not interaction tracking. ItemPageScreen.kt (lines 99, 352, 379) only passes the item key to the onItemClicked callback, and ItemInfoFragment.kt:57 routes it to openItem, which pushes a fragment. ItemsFragment.kt:46-51 opens the item page and sets a viewed flag through updateViewedByUserFieldForItem, which ends in a local Room update: ItemsDao.kt:29 "UPDATE ItemsTable SET viewedByUser = 1 WHERE name =:name". The item page itself loads from bundled assets (GetItemInfoUseCase.kt:107 readText via res.getAssets, line 111 file:///android_asset image), so opening an item makes no network request. No analytics or crash SDK is present: build files and libs.versions.toml have no Firebase, Crashlytics, AppMetrica, Sentry, Amplitude or ad SDK (the only Google Play services entry is play-services-instantapps), and no logEvent/trackEvent call exists. The custom Logger keeps entries in an in-memory SharedFlow (LoggerImpl.kt:14-23), and its main-source consumers only display it: the drawer log list (DrawerFragment.kt:231), the XO log state (XoViewModel.kt:44) and logcat (CameraFragment.kt:100), so none uploads it. Tapping play on an ability sound (ItemInfoFragment.onPlayClicked) streams a static audioUrl, which is a content fetch and carries no interaction payload.
findings.recommendation: No Data Safety declaration is needed for App interactions. Keep the viewed flag local. If an analytics or crash SDK is added later, update the Play Data safety form first, because the current form declares no data collected.

findings.issue_summary: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION are declared for every Android version, although the code only needs location below Android 13.
findings.evidence: AndroidManifest.xml lines 11-16 declare ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION with android:required="true" and no android:maxSdkVersion. GamesFragment.kt line 50 uses NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES on API 33+ and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION only below it, and manifest lines 9-10 already mark NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES as neverForLocation. So on Android 13+ the location permissions are declared but never requested or needed. A downgrade to COARSE alone is not an option, because Wi-Fi Direct needs FINE below API 33. No location API (LocationManager, FusedLocation, getLastKnownLocation, requestLocationUpdates), SSID read or IP geo-lookup was found in the source, so this is excess declared scope, not location collection.
findings.recommendation: Add android:maxSdkVersion="32" to both location <uses-permission> entries and drop android:required="true", so the permissions apply only to Android 12/12L (minSdk is 31). Check the merged release manifest afterwards to confirm no other module or library declares them without the limit.

findings.issue_summary: On Android 12/12L the Games screen requests location as soon as it opens, with no explanation, and requests FINE without COARSE.
findings.evidence: GamesFragment.kt lines 64-67 call permissionRequest.launch(wifiDirectPermission) from onViewCreated on first entry, with no dialog or rationale before it, and the mix/ui strings.xml has no permission or location explanation text. The app is a Dota 2 helper, so its purpose does not imply location. This stays a suggestion because the disclosure row of the matrix requires foreground tracking and none exists: location is only the OS gate for Wi-Fi Direct on API 31-32, and the app reads no location. Separately, line 51 uses the single-permission RequestPermission contract with FINE only. Android documentation says that for apps targeting 31+ a FINE request without COARSE can be ignored by the system and logged as an error, so the prompt may never appear and Wi-Fi Direct may stay off on these versions. This was not checked on a device. The FINE request in feature\games\xo\demo AppPermission.kt belongs to a demo app and is not part of the release app.
findings.recommendation: On API 31-32, show a short explanation before the system prompt saying that Android needs the location permission to find nearby phones over Wi-Fi Direct and that the app does not read or store location. Trigger the request when the user starts nearby play instead of on screen open if that fits the flow. Request FINE and COARSE together with RequestMultiplePermissions, then verify on an Android 12 device or emulator.

findings.issue_summary: SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM is declared for reminder code that nothing calls.
findings.evidence: core\common-android AndroidManifest.xml line 4 declares SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM. USE_EXACT_ALARM is not declared, so the restricted permission rule in the policy matrix is not triggered. RemindersManager has no references outside its own file, so startReminder (setAlarmClock on line 37) is never called. AlarmReceiver.onReceive and BootReceiver.onReceive (lines 49-51 and 56-59) do no real work, and the app does not declare RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED. The app has no alarm, timer or calendar purpose that would need exact timing.
findings.recommendation: Remove the SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM permission, the AlarmReceiver and BootReceiver manifest entries and RemindersManager.kt, in line with the project rule to delete unused code. If reminders return later, use WorkManager or inexact AlarmManager scheduling.
